Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the judgment and award dated 09.01.2024 passed in MVC No.6018/2021 on the file of the XII Additional Small Causes Judge and ACMM, MACT, Bengaluru, (SCCH-8) for enhancing the compensation.
2.

entities.text: XII Additional Small Causes Judge and ACMM, MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.1/Insurance Company.
The ranks of the parties are retained as per Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
NC: 2026:KHC:7237 HC-KAR 3.
The petitioner/injured claimant met with an accident on 06.12.2021 and filed petition before the Tribunal for compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-.
The Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted an amount of Rs.4,08,922/-.
The Tribunal granted interest at the rate of 6% p.a., on amount of Rs.3,78,922/- from the date of filing the petition till the date of realization, (No interest on future medical expenditure).
Being aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is filed.
4. It is stated that the petitioner/injured sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized for a period of three days as an inpatient.
He has shortening of the lower limb by 2 Cm.
Accordingly, the doctor assessed the permanent disability of the lower limb at 42.43% and to whole body 14%.

The petitioner/injured requires another surgery for delayed union, exchange nailing and bone grafting,
the estimated cost of which is Rs.1,00,000/-.
The petitioner/injured was aged 18 years and was working as a Cable Operator, earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

But the Tribunal granted meagre amounts under the NC: 2026:KHC:7237 HC-KAR other heads and awarded inadequate Sri Shaik Shameer vs Acko General Insurance Company Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199214849/
2 compensation.

sentences.text: Therefore, requested for enhancement of the compensation.
5. Learned counsel for respondent No.1/insurance company stated that the petitioner/injured was aged 18 years and in the course of time, the fractures would unite.
As such, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the disability at 10%, which needs no interference.
It is further stated that the petitioner/injured has not filed any records to show that he underwent surgery for removal of the implants.
But the Tribunal granted future medical expenses and it needs interference.
Though it is contended that the petitioner/injured was working as a Cable Operator and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, he has not filed any income proof.
As he met with an accident in the year 2021, his notional income is to be taken at Rs.15,000/- per month, as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The petitioner/injured was aged 18 years and the applicable multiplier is '18'.

As per Ex.P.5-wound certificate, the petitioner/injured sustained the following injuries:
 i. Abrasion over right knee joint  NC: 2026:KHC:7237 HC-KAR  ii. Tenderness over right femur iii. X-ray shows-comminuted right fracture 6.
The petitioner/injured examined the treated doctor as PW.2.
He stated that the petitioner/injured sustained a comminuted fracture of the mid-shaft of the right femur and the fractures are not yet united.
The Tribunal has observed that the petitioner was young, the fracture would reunite or even if it is malunited, it would not affect his earning capacity.
Accordingly, the Tribunal assessed the disability at 10%.

It is further stated that the petitioner underwent surgery for the right femur,
wherein closed reduction and interlocking nail was applied.
The doctor further stated that the petitioner requires another surgery, the estimated cost of which is Rs.1,00,000/-.
He assessed the permanent disability of the lower limb at 42.43% and that of the whole body is 14.14%.
He also disclosed that, as the injuries are permanent in nature, the petitioner would not be able to engage in heavy manual work.

This Court finds it reasonable to take 1/3rd of 42.43% i.e., 14% instead of 10%
as assessed by the Tribunal.

Accordingly, the loss of future earning capacity comes to Rs.4,53,600/-
NC: 2026:KHC:7237 HC-KAR (Rs.15,000  12  18  14%).

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.77,122/-
towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.
The petitioner/injured was hospitalized for a period of three days.

Considering the nature of injuries, the medical evidence and the shortening of the right lower limb by 2 cm, this Court finds it reasonable to grant a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- towards transportation,

Considering the medical evidence, this Court finds it reasonable to enhance the compensation towards future medical expenses to Rs.50,000/- instead of Rs.30,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

iv. Respondent No.1/Insurance Company has already deposited the award amount before the Tribunal.
Therefore, respondent No.1/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.3,21,800/- along with the interest at the rate of 6% within one month from the date of this order.
